subtopic: Accumulation precision / Mixed precision Tensor Core
learningObjective: Enumerate the correct properties of mixed-precision Tensor Core GEMM: FP16/BF16 inputs with FP32 accumulator.
stem: Regarding mixed-precision GEMM on NVIDIA Tensor Cores (e.g., FP16 or BF16 inputs with an FP32 accumulator), which of the following statements are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Storing weights and activations in FP16/BF16 halves memory footprint and doubles memory bandwidth utilization relative to FP32 for the load path.
Because the accumulator is FP32, the compute throughput of mixed-precision GEMM matches pure FP32 GEMM on Tensor Cores.
The accumulator dtype (FP32) determines the effective precision of the running sum, mitigating overflow and catastrophic cancellation compared to FP16/BF16 accumulation.
Downcasting the FP32 accumulator to FP16/BF16 on write introduces a rounding error per output element that can affect training stability if not accounted for.

explanation: Options A, C, D are correct; option B is incorrect. A (Correct): bandwidth halving is central to Tensor Core speed-up. B (Wrong): mixed-precision Tensor Core is 8-16× faster than FP32 GEMM. C (Correct): accumulator dtype drives numerical stability. D (Correct): downcast rounding is a real, per-element error source.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: bandwidth halving is central to Tensor Core speed-up.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: mixed-precision Tensor Core is 8-16× faster than FP32 GEMM.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: accumulator dtype drives numerical stability.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: downcast rounding is a real, per-element error source.

assumptions: The GEMM uses standard cuBLAS or CUTLASS Tensor Core kernels.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP32 accumulator eliminates all numerical concerns — subnormal handling and non-associative order still matter.
Does not imply switching output to FP32 always improves accuracy meaningfully — many workloads see negligible difference.

performanceClaim.scope: Mixed-precision Tensor Core GEMM numerical properties and bandwidth
